sections.html:
Kearney is the Buffalo County seat, built beside the Platte River on Interstate 80, with the Union Pacific main line through town. The population stood at 34,782 on July 1, 2025, spread over roughly 13 square miles. Health care, education, retail and manufacturing anchor the local economy.

Commutes average 16 minutes in the county, so when you describe the house, give drive times to the interstate and to the university.

sections.h2: Renting near the University of Nebraska at Kearney
sections.html:
UNK is a 235-acre residential campus and one of the larger employers in the city. Central Community College also has a branch campus in Kearney. Homes near campus are often rentals.

  • If you own a rental, gather the leases and security deposit records before you talk to a buyer.
  • Give a buyer copies of the leases and deposit amounts early so nothing surprises them at closing.
  • Tenants stay in place unless the lease says otherwise, so check the end dates.

sections.h2: Weather and your roof, siding and concrete
sections.html:
Kearney averages 25.56 inches of precipitation and 21.8 inches of snow a year. May is the wettest month at 4.40 inches, and February is the snowiest at 5.6 inches. Hot summers and cold, dry winters stress roofing, siding and concrete flatwork, and a buyer's inspector will note all three.

Before deciding how to sell a house that needs a new roof or furnace, collect a written bid. It gives you a real number to weigh against a cash offer.

Kearney's Development Services Department handles permits, code enforcement, inspections and planning and zoning in one place. Building Services checks work against the adopted zoning, building, electrical and plumbing codes. Code Enforcement takes complaints by phone at (308) 233-3235 or through the Access Kearney app.

  • Find out if earlier projects on the house had permits.
  • Before you accept an offer, request a list of open permits or violations for your address.
  • The city code is on Municode if you want to read the chapters yourself.

Call the department to ask whether any sale-time inspection applies to your house.

sections.h2: Deeds, copies and property tax in Buffalo County
sections.html:
The Buffalo County Register of Deeds records deeds in the courthouse in Kearney, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays. Copies cost $0.50 a page. A free Property Fraud Alert from the same office sends you an email or text whenever a document is recorded under your name.

OfficeHandlesPhone
Register of DeedsDeed recording, copies, fraud alert(308) 236-1239
TreasurerProperty tax bills, tax sales (PO Box 1270, Kearney)(308) 236-1250
Code EnforcementComplaints, open violations(308) 233-3235

For delinquency dates, ask the Treasurer about your parcel. State law sets May 1 and September 1 in counties under 100,000 people.

sections.h2: Watch for the Recorded Deed Notice mailer
sections.html: A mail scam asks for $86 and calls itself a "Recorded Deed Notice." The Register of Deeds says to send no money. You can get a copy of your own recorded deed at the courthouse for $0.50 a page.

Kearney sellers pay the state documentary stamp tax when the deed is recorded. Under LB1067 the rate climbs from $2.32 to $3.32 per $1,000 starting July 18, 2026, and the higher rate lasts through December 31, 2031. Treat it as a closing cost.

sections.h2: The disclosure form and its timing
sections.html:
The disclosure statement must reach the buyer on or before the effective date of the binding contract, and the buyer must acknowledge receipt in writing. If you learn something before then that makes the statement wrong, update it.

Fill the form out at the start, not after you accept an offer. It covers appliances, the electrical, heating and cooling, water and sewer systems, defects that affect value, hazardous substances, title conditions and carbon monoxide alarm compliance.

A missed form does not void the transfer. The buyer can still sue for actual damages and attorney's fees, so complete it every time.

sections.h2: Preparing a Kearney house for buyers
sections.html:
Begin with what an inspector notices in the first ten minutes: roof, furnace, water heater, electrical panel, and the concrete steps and drive. Handle the cheap fixes yourself and get one written bid for anything large, so you know the true cost.

  • Put warranties, receipts and permit records in a single folder.
  • Ask Development Services about open permits or code violations.
  • Choose early between repairing, giving the buyer a credit, or selling as is.
  • If tenants live there, warn them a sale is coming and ask how they would like showings arranged.

Someone paying cash tends to inspect less and does not have a lender's repair list to satisfy, which can save weeks.

A title company or attorney searches title, clears liens, prorates the property tax for the year and drafts the deed. You sign, and the Register of Deeds records the deed at the courthouse. The state stamp tax is due at recording and comes out of your proceeds.

Bring photo ID, keys, garage openers and any warranty papers still in force. An inherited house adds one step: the court papers showing your authority to sell go to the title company beforehand. After the sale, sign up for the Property Fraud Alert so you hear if anything is later recorded under your name.

The Treasurer bills property tax, and delinquent parcels go to tax sale. Settle the current bill before closing so the title company works from a clean number.

With a cash buyer there is no appraisal and no lender underwriting, and the repair-request round after an inspection mostly disappears. The disclosure form, the deed, the recording and the tax proration all stay. Weigh any cash offer against your net on a listing after commissions, repairs and months of carrying costs. No price is promised, and asking for an offer commits you to nothing.

faqs.q: Who records a deed in Kearney, Nebraska?
faqs.a: The Buffalo County Register of Deeds, in the courthouse in Kearney. The phone is (308) 236-1239 and the email is deeds@buffalocounty.ne.gov.

faqs.q: What is the Nebraska documentary stamp tax rate for a Kearney sale?
faqs.a: $3.32 per $1,000 beginning July 18, 2026, and the higher rate lasts through December 31, 2031.

faqs.q: What is the Recorded Deed Notice scam in Buffalo County?
faqs.a: A mailer asking for about $86 for a copy of a recorded deed. Copies are $0.50 a page at the courthouse, so do not send money.

faqs.q: Does Kearney require a point-of-sale inspection for a house?
faqs.a: Call Kearney Development Services at the number on the city's code enforcement page to confirm.

faqs.q: Which school district covers most of Kearney?
faqs.a: Kearney Public Schools, which operates preschools, ten elementary schools, two middle schools and Kearney High School.
